name: Gnomish Tools
summary: Along Durotar's coast, Gnomish Tools lie among the wrecks of Proudmoore's fleet. The Horde seeks the salvaged devices to study Alliance engineering and adapt its innovations for survival.

sections.title: Sunken Salvage
sections.body: Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet brought vast supplies of modern equipment to Durotar. Proudmoore led Kul Tiras and Alliance forces to its shores, with sophisticated gear made by their gnomish allies aboard. After the fleet was destroyed along the Scuttle Coast, east of Tiragarde Keep, the delicate mechanical kits sank beneath the waves. Waterproof toolboxes still lie among the rotting timbers and barnacle-encrusted hulls in the shallows.

sections.title: Eyes in Orgrimmar
sections.body: Gar'Thok, who oversees Razor Hill, sent Horde scouts to recover tools from the watery grave of Proudmoore's navy. The orcs know humans and gnomes are skilled in engineering, especially siege engines, shipwrighting, and clockwork mechanics. They send the kits by caravan to craftsmen and scholars in Orgrimmar. There, the Horde means to study Alliance contraptions, learn to counter enemy war machines, and adapt foreign innovations for its own survival.

faq.q: Why are gnomish tools lying off the coast of Durotar?
aliases: how did tools get in durotar
faq.answer: Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet carried the tools when Kul Tiras assaulted Durotar. When the armada was shattered and sunk along the Scuttle Coast, east of Tiragarde Keep, its naval cargo settled on the ocean floor.

faq.q: Why does the Horde want these tools?
faq.answer: Gar'Thok of Razor Hill wants the tools recovered and sent to Orgrimmar. Studying the intricate mechanical knowledge of Alliance engineers can help the Horde understand enemy machines and build better gear of its own.
The tools lie in toolboxes scattered in and around sunken wreckage along Durotar's Scuttle Coast, just east of Tiragarde Keep. Many rest underwater or across half-submerged broken hulls.

angles.text: As an engineer, you can study these kits for insight into the precise craft of Alliance tinkers, clockwork assemblies, and miniaturization.
As a member of the Horde, you can help recover lost Alliance equipment for study. Learning enemy designs and foreign mechanisms can help the Horde defend against future naval invasions.
